Yakushima.authority: Environment Ministry / kyoju.biodic.go.jp giant-tree database (same national register already imported for Hiroshima/Sapporo/Kobe/Nagoya/Kamakura/Nikko/Nara per data/register-scouting.json's Japan entry), PLUS the Agency for Cultural Affairs national Natural Monument database (data/registers/japan-bunkacho.json, already held).
Yakushima.url: https://kyoju.biodic.go.jp/?_action=gtsearch, run via scripts/jp_kyoju.py --prefecture 46 (Kagoshima, which includes Yakushima-cho)
Yakushima.licence: PDL 1.0, already proven in OPEN_DATA_SURVEY.md 2026-08-04 for this exact database (Admin-authored rows only, per the field-based filter jp_kyoju.py already applies). No new licence work needed.
Yakushima.fields: species, girth (幹周), height (樹高), a vitality field (健全度, health condition), confirmation date. NO coordinates: this database gives prefecture/municipality/address only, same caveat already recorded for the whole Japan entry, so pinning individual Yakushima cedars (the Jomon Sugi, Kigen Sugi, Yakusugi land) is a separate job per tree, same as Hiroshima's leads file.
Yakushima.count: Confirmed by running the script live this pass: prefecture 46 (Kagoshima) returns 975 records total (crawl started, ~100 fetched before this pass stopped it to stay in budget; not filtered to Yakushima-cho yet). The Agency for Cultural Affairs national register (already imported, data/registers/japan-bunkacho.json) carries exactly ONE Yakushima-area entry, '屋久島スギ原始林' (Yakushima Sugi Primeval Forest, a whole-forest area designation at 30.3287,130.5042), which is an ensemble/wood and fails the collectible-point test on its own; it is NOT the Jomon Sugi or another single named tree, so it cannot be used as a per-tree register entry.
Yakushima.note: Two things settle this. (1) The mechanism already exists and is proven: python3 scripts/jp_kyoju.py --prefecture 46 --out data/leads/yakushima.json is the exact next command, same licence and same script already trusted for seven other cities. It ran live this pass (55s, reached page 2 of the results before being stopped to respect the pass timebox) and returned real records, confirming the endpoint answers for Kagoshima prefecture. (2) The famous named cedars (Jomon Sugi, Kigen Sugi, Wilson's Stump) will very likely appear inside those 975 records by name or address, but the database gives no coordinates for any of them, so a follow-up verify pass still needs to place each one from tourism/park sources (Forestry Agency Yakushima Kokumin-rin trail materials, the observation-deck coordinates published for Jomon Sugi specifically) the way Hiroshima's pass separated register data from pinning. This is register-backed verify work (rung 4b in CLAUDE.md, ~0.4k tokens/tree), not from-zero research. Kagoshima's server was noticeably slower than the prefectures already crawled (roughly 5-8s per page fetch versus the faster prefectures), so a future pull should expect a longer run, not a hang; it did not time out, it was simply mid-crawl when this pass moved on.

Cyprus.authority: Republic of Cyprus Department of Forests (Τμήμα Δασών), Ministry of Agriculture, Natural Resources and Environment, published on the National Open Data Portal (data.gov.cy)
Cyprus.url: https://data.gov.cy/el/dataset/memonomena-dentra-mnimeia-tis-fysis-ektos-ton-kratikon-dason ; direct file https://data.gov.cy/sites/default/files/TreeMonumentsOutsideStateForests.csv (fetched clean via curl, 82 lines incl header)
Cyprus.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated directly on the dataset page. Proven by fetch, not by search summary.
Cyprus.fields: Species (Greek common name), District (Λευκωσίας/Λεμεσού/Πάφου/Λάρνακας/Αμμοχώστου), Village, circumference at chest height (m), height (m), AGE IN YEARS, official proclamation date. No coordinates, only village + district, so location_precision stays approximate until each tree is geocoded to its village. No vitality field.
Cyprus.count: 81 trees nationwide (this dataset is explicitly 'outside state forests' only; Forestry Dept press material cited separately says roughly 68 more isolated trees plus 2 groups sit inside state forests, but no second dataset for those was found on the portal this pass, so treat that subset as unscouted rather than covered). By district: Limassol 31, Paphos 28, Nicosia 13, Larnaca 5, Famagusta 4. Zero in Kyrenia/Famagusta-north, i.e. the Turkish-administered area: this Republic-of-Cyprus dataset almost certainly does not and cannot cover the north, which sits outside the Republic's Forestry Department jurisdiction; whether Northern Cyprus keeps any equivalent list was not checked this pass and stays unscouted.
Cyprus.note: Strong find, same tier as Bratislava/Bari/Lyon: real licence, real age field (rare), fetched and spot-read directly rather than trusted from a search summary. One register pitfall worth flagging for whoever imports it: several age values look suspiciously patterned (313, 513, 213, 133, 1508, 708...) which may be 'years since a fixed reference date' rather than a clean age-at-designation figure; sanity-check a few against known trees (e.g. the Apaisia terebinth widely reported as Cyprus's oldest tree, a candidate row here as Τρέμιθος/Apaisia at 1,508) before trusting the column at face value, per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's register-pitfalls section. Next step for a build pass: import as data/registers/cyprus-forestry-monuments.json, then geocode by village for pinning, same shape as other village-only registers.

Crete.authority: Greek Ministry of Environment and Energy / regional Dasarcheio (forestry service), designation 'Διατηρητέο Μνημείο της Φύσης' (Preserved Natural Monument) under Law 998/1979 (originally Legislative Decree 86/1969).
Crete.url: https://el.wikipedia.org/wiki/Διατηρητέα_μνημεία_της_φύσης (fetched; a prose/list article citing ΦΕΚ gazette numbers, not a data table); no data.gov.gr or ypen.gov.gr dataset found for this designation this pass
Crete.licence: No data licence to prove: there is no dataset. The designations exist only as individual ΦΕΚ (Government Gazette) publications and prose lists (el.wikipedia.org's own article on the topic cites ΦΕΚ numbers, not a database).
Crete.fields: n/a, no register exists as data. The prose article names a handful of Crete entries (Cretan Cephalanthero at Kamarai, two oaks at Korfes, two olives at Almyropotamos, an evergreen plane in Heraklion, cypress forests and a plane/elm in Chania) but with no coordinates, age or girth given, just place names.
Crete.count: roughly 6-7 named natural-monument entries for Crete in the national list, none near Heraklion/Chania town centre itself per the article's wording (Korfes, Almyropotamos, Vlatos, Palaiochora, Aidona Kalambaka are all outlying villages).
Crete.note: The national designation is real but is not a usable register: it is ΦΕΚ prose, not data. The much stronger route for Crete, named in the brief and confirmed this pass, is the Olive Tree of Vouves (Ano Vouves, near Kolymvari, roughly 25 km from Chania): a single, famous, individually documented tree with its own museum (visited by 20,000+ people/year), a peer-reviewed genetics paper (PMC8620074) discussing its origin, and an official 'natural heritage monument' declaration by the Region of Crete. Age is genuinely disputed across sources (2,000 to 4,000 years, no agreed dating method for olives), which is exactly the kind of range BRIEF_RESEARCH.md says to report honestly rather than pick a winner. This is a from-zero verify candidate, not a register import: two independent sources already surfaced (Wikipedia's own dedicated 'Olive tree of Vouves' article, the museum's own ABEA.gr page, the PMC paper) and it clears the collectible-point and access bars easily (public museum site). Recommend a verify pass name this tree directly rather than searching further.

Oahu.authority: City & County of Honolulu, Department of Parks and Recreation, Division of Urban Forestry, publishing the 'Exceptional Trees On Oahu' dataset on the Honolulu Open Data Portal (Socrata). Despite the name, confirmed by querying the live data (not a search summary) that it carries entries tagged for Kauai, Maui, the Big Island and Moloka'i/Lanai too, not Oahu alone.
Oahu.url: https://data.honolulu.gov/Recreation/Exceptional-Trees-On-Oahu/84fd-3fzf ; queried directly via the Socrata API, e.g. https://data.honolulu.gov/resource/84fd-3fzf.json?$limit=5 (curl -m 20, HTTP 200, real rows)
Oahu.licence: CC0 1.0 Universal (Public Domain Dedication), confirmed by fetching the dataset's own metadata API (https://data.honolulu.gov/api/views/84fd-3fzf.json), licenseId 'CC0_10', attribution 'Department of Parks and Recreation'. The best licence found on this whole pass: no attribution even required.
Oahu.fields: species (scientific_name, common_name), height, diameter_in, trunk_circumference (girth, though many rows read 'null'), a live TREE CONDITION / vitality field ('Excellent', 'Good' etc, coded), crown spread, land_use, a plain-English location_description ('Foster Botanical Garden, 180 N. Vineyard Blvd.', 'Schofield Barracks...'), an island code, and TREE-LEVEL LATITUDE/LONGITUDE on every row queried. No age field, so age here would need the growth-rate/girth route or stay an honest gap per BRIEF_RESEARCH.md.
Oahu.count: ~240 of the 339 statewide rows are coded Oahu ('O' 236 + 'Oahu' spelled out 4). Includes central-Honolulu landmarks by name (Foster Botanical Garden, Queen's Medical Center, Ala Moana Beach Park), so a meaningful share sits in or near town; exact walking-distance count not run this pass.
Oahu.note: This is the best find of the pass: coordinates, condition/vitality and a public-domain licence together, which no European register scouted so far has matched all three of. One caveat worth flagging for a build pass: some rows describe a GROVE ('Grove [11]', a baobab grove at Ala Moana) rather than one trunk, which fails the collectible-point rule and needs filtering per row, same discipline as Lyon's PLU-H layer. Also worth checking before import: whether Hawai'i County (Big Island) and Maui/Kauai maintain their OWN separate, richer registries alongside feeding this one (the brief's search for a Hawaii County ArcGIS 'Exceptional Trees' layer, id 59, 404'd this pass at gis.hawaiicounty.gov/arcgis/rest/services/COHGIS_Public/COHGIS_Public/MapServer/59, so that specific URL is stale or renamed, not proof no county-level layer exists). Next step for a build pass: import as data/registers/hawaii-exceptional-trees.json directly from the Socrata endpoint (no scraping needed, it is a real API), then cluster per island.
